title: Can the totient product formula φ(n) = n·∏_{p|n}(1-1/p) be formalized directl...
description: Can the totient product formula φ(n) = n·∏_{p|n}(1-1/p) be formalized directly in Lean using Mathlib's prime factorization infrastructure? This would generalize totient_prime_pow by expressing φ as a product over distinct prime divisors.

problemStatement.formal: Formalize Euler's totient product formula using Nat.factorization and product over prime factors.
problemStatement.plain: Express phi(n) as a product over prime-power contributions, then derive rational-form and density interpretations.
whyMatters: The result connects multiplicativity of the totient function to Lean's canonical prime-factorization API.
It gives concrete reusable formulas for computations and density-style interpretations of phi(n) / n.

proven: totient_factorization_formula proves the prime-factorization product formula for Nat.totient.
totient_rational_formula rewrites the same result as a rational product over prime divisors.
totient_div_primes_formula and totient_from_multiplicativity connect the formula to multiplicativity.
totient_prime_power_contribution isolates the contribution of a prime power.
totient_twelve_via_formula and totient_360 verify concrete examples.
totient_density and totient_density_same_support package the phi(n) / n density interpretation.
knownResults.goal: Expose the completed factorization-based totient formula and its computational corollaries.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: All forms of the product formula proved. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
insights: Mathlib already contains Nat.totient_eq_prod_factorization, Nat.totient_eq_mul_prod_factors, and Nat.totient_eq_div_primeFactors_mul — all three standard forms of the product formula
The product formula is a direct consequence of multiplicativity + FTA + prime power formula; proved via Finsupp.prod_congr
Totient density φ(n)/n = ∏(1-1/p) depends only on the radical (set of prime divisors), not on the exponents
builtItems: totient_factorization_formula: φ(n) = n.factorization.prod (fun p k => p^(k-1)*(p-1))
totient_rational_formula: (φ(n) : ℚ) = n * ∏ p in primeFactors, (1 - 1/p)
